- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) mid-period, model may lag in adjusting downward; apply early correction if sentiment shifts sharply.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; smooth out extremes by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before forecasting.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “up-down” cycles, model tends to overreact to recent lows — dampen forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is weak.
